## Discovery & Translational Science

* **[Biotech]** **Intellia Therapeutics pinpoints mechanism behind gene-editing liver toxicity** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/daraxonrasib-compassionate-use-intellia-arrowhead-cspc-vedanta/827186/)
  * Intellia Therapeutics identified the biological pathway driving an increased risk of liver toxicity observed in patients receiving one of its experimental gene-editing candidates.

* **EPAS1 loss-of-function variants drive primary resistance to antiangiogenic TKIs in hepatocellular carcinoma** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.05.26358954)
  * Multi-cohort integration revealed that germline adaptive loss-of-function variants in *EPAS1* (HIF-2α), enriched in high-altitude populations, reduce endothelial *EPAS1* expression under hypoxia.
  * Reduced *EPAS1* expression promotes primary resistance to antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) through a dysregulated HIF-2/STC2 signaling axis.

* **Novel gain-of-function mutation in dysferlin triggers NLRP3 inflammasome activation and autoinflammation** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.04.26358821)
  * Researchers identified a de novo gain-of-function mutation in dysferlin (*DYSF* p.P1449L) in pediatric patients presenting with severe systemic autoinflammation and sterile lung abscesses.
  * The mutation enhances COP-I binding and causes dysferlin retention in the ER-Golgi, disrupting myeloid membrane homeostasis and triggering ectopic perinuclear NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and IL-1β release.

* **Rational design yields Gᵢ-biased CB1 agonists for non-opioid analgesia** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42568023/)
  * Structure-based design yielded Gᵢ-protein-biased cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1) agonists engineered to maintain central pain attenuation while mitigating pathway-specific adverse effects.

* **Puerarin mitigates doxorubicin-induced endothelial ferroptosis via DDAH II target engagement** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42567347/)
  * Pharmacological targeting of dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolase II (DDAH II) with puerarin corrected ADMA/NOS pathway dysregulation, preventing doxorubicin-induced endothelial damage and ferroptosis.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **Revolution Medicines sees strong compassionate-use demand for daraxonrasib** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/daraxonrasib-compassionate-use-intellia-arrowhead-cspc-vedanta/827186/)
  * More than 2,000 patients with pancreatic cancer have received Revolution Medicines' RAS inhibitor daraxonrasib under an expanded access/compassionate use program.
  * The drug is undergoing expedited FDA review for pancreatic cancer, with commercial projections reaching $1.1 billion by 2027.

* **First-in-human trial confirms feasibility of shear-responsive NeoCast biomaterial** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42567700/)
  * A prospective first-in-human trial evaluated NeoCast, a next-generation shear-responsive liquid embolic biomaterial, demonstrating successful intravascular delivery and acute occlusion parameters.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Metformin demonstrates neutral long-term cognitive impact in DPPOS trial** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.05.26359234)
  * Long-term follow-up of 1,483 participants in the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study (DPPOS) evaluated cognitive trajectories over a mean metformin exposure of 15.5 years.
  * Randomization to metformin compared with placebo or intensive lifestyle intervention produced no significant difference in the incidence of cognitive impairment syndromes or executive/memory decline.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Design details published for Phase 3 HPS-4/TIMI 65/ORION-4 trial of inclisiran** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42567431/)
  * Trial leadership published the study design and baseline demographics for the Phase 3 HPS-4/TIMI 65/ORION-4 outcome trial evaluating long-term cardiovascular event reduction with the siRNA therapy inclisiran in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Biotech]** **FDA grants accelerated approval to Replimune's Tudriqev for advanced melanoma** [FDA](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/ongoing-cancer-accelerated-approvals)
  * The FDA granted accelerated approval to Tudriqev (vusolimogene oderparepvec-wtpg) in combination with nivolumab for adults with unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma progressing on prior PD-1 blockade.
  * Full approval remains contingent upon clinical benefit confirmation in the ongoing randomized Phase 3 IGNYTE-3 trial (NCT06264180).

* **FDA issues EUA for CLiK Extra wound spray to control New World screwworm** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issues-emergency-use-authorization-drug-prevent-new-world-screwworm-multiple-species-including)
  * The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization for CLiK Extra (dicyclanil topical suspension) to prevent New World screwworm infestations (myiasis) across multiple livestock and wildlife species.

* **Baxter issues voluntary recall for Cefazolin in Dextrose Injection** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/baxter-issues-voluntary-nationwide-recall-cefazolin-dextrose-injection-usp-2g-100ml20mg-ml-single)
  * Baxter International initiated a voluntary recall for one lot of Cefazolin in Dextrose Injection, USP (2g/100 mL) following a report of particulate matter identified as cardboard in single-dose infusion bags.

* **FDA releases final ICH M11 guidance on electronic structured protocols** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/m11-clinical-electronic-structured-harmonised-protocol)
  * The FDA published final guidance including standardized templates and technical specifications for ICH M11, establishing international standards for electronic clinical trial protocol formatting and data exchange.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Biotech]** **Latigo Biotherapeutics raises $346M in upsized IPO for non-opioid pain pipeline** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/latigo-ipo-public-biotech-pain-drug-nasdaq/827300/)
  * Latigo Biotherapeutics priced 19.2 million shares at $18 to gross $345.6 million, supporting clinical development of its non-opioid pain program.
  * The pricing occurred alongside three other clinical-stage IPOs this week: BlossomHill Therapeutics ($150 million), Braveheart Bio ($382.5 million), and Attovia Therapeutics ($289 million).

* **[Biotech]** **Industry commentary flags pipeline reprioritization toward pan-RAS targets** [X / @JacobPlieth](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2085724502214820318)
  * Reports indicate clinical-stage pivots away from selective pan-KRAS inhibitor assets in favor of broader pan-RAS molecular approaches.

## Public Health & Policy

* **NIH plans to bar international visa holders from K99/R00 career awards** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/07/nih-k99-pathways-independence-awards-scientists-on-visas-barred/)
  * The National Institutes of Health plans to restrict eligibility for K99/R00 Pathway to Independence Awards, preventing international postdoctoral researchers on visas from accessing the grant mechanism.

* **Transmission modeling attributes influenza B/Yamagata extinction to low basic reproduction number** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.22.26358639)
  * Mathematical modeling of global influenza dynamics suggests the apparent post-2020 disappearance of the B/Yamagata lineage was primarily caused by its lower baseline R₀ relative to B/Victoria during pandemic non-pharmaceutical interventions.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Fluffy LDL particles and cardiovascular risk | Jim Otvos, Ph.D.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Ee1PuwnX5Tw) -- Peter Attia MD
        - LDL particle number (LDL-P) provides cardiovascular risk assessment that LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) misses when discordance exists between the two markers.
        - The concept that large, "fluffy" LDL particles are benign is disproven, with specific genetic conditions demonstrating their atherogenic potential.
        - An NMR-derived score measures insulin resistance and can predict type 2 diabetes years before elevated blood glucose is detectable.
        - GlycA is highlighted as an NMR marker for chronic inflammation that yields a more stable signal than standard clinical hs-CRP assays.
    - [HIPAA, Healthcare VCs & AI Startups | HealthTech #DadJokes](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Vzknz239ZLo) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - The clip uses a healthtech "dad joke" format targeting healthcare founders, investors, and AI developers.
        - It highlights common friction points in healthcare startup fundraising and HIPAA compliance.
        - Content specifically parodies Hippocratic AI and trends within the digital health startup ecosystem.
    - [The AI Hype Went Too Far](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lvJSznAaDps) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Features Stephanie Davis discussing the prevalence of "AI washing" in digital health startup pitches.
        - Highlights rising investor fatigue caused by exaggerated claims surrounding artificial intelligence in healthcare.
        - Explains why venture capital investors have developed a lack of trust in healthcare AI startup presentations.
- Pure Science
    - [How Does Touch Lead To Pain Or Pleasure? | PODCAST: The Joy of Why](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RyXzgj7b7xQ) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Neuroscientist Ishmail Abdus-Saboor discusses efforts to map the somatosensory system to understand tactile pain and pleasure processing.
        - Highlights the methodological challenges of quantifying pain and building pain scales in laboratory animals without objective biomarkers.
        - Explores touch as a social and emotional signal using optogenetics to investigate gentle touch and social bonding.
        - Features research on naked mole rats, a species with minimal pain sensitivity that relies on touch to navigate social colony structures.
    - [Earth’s Core Is Leaking: Here's the Evidence](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/kt3783nSJWs) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Presents geophysical evidence indicating that primordial material from Earth's core is migrating toward the planet's surface.
        - Suggests that continent-sized structures anchored at the core-mantle boundary may participate in this material transport.
        - Cites associated research published in Nature investigating deep Earth mantle dynamics and geochemistry.
